plain_english_title: Musculoskeletal System Guide: Painful Motion, Multi-Code Knee Stacking, Implants, Amputations & Foot Rules
what_this_means: Orthopedic claims are among the most common—and most frequently misrated—conditions in VA compensation. Beyond basic goniometer degree tables in 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a, VA raters must account for painful motion warranting at least the minimum compensable rating (§ 4.59), additional functional loss from pain, weakness, fatigue, and flare-ups (§§ 4.40 and 4.45), dominant ('Major') vs. non-dominant ('Minor') upper-extremity rules (§ 4.69), separate knee ratings when instability and limited motion coexist, prosthetic joint replacement minimums and convalescence (Diagnostic Codes 5051–5056), and post-February 7, 2021 foot codes like Plantar Fasciitis (Diagnostic Code 5269).
record_clues: A 0% joint rating when the VA examination noted objective painful motion—violating 38 C.F.R. § 4.59's rule requiring at least the minimum compensable percentage (10% for most joints; 20% for either shoulder under Diagnostic Code 5201 when arm elevation stops at shoulder level / 90 degrees).

A knee injury with documented giving-way/instability AND limited bending (flexion) or straightening (extension) folded into a single knee code instead of separate ratings under Diagnostic Codes 5257, 5260, and 5261 (VAOPGCPREC 23-97, 9-98, and Lyles v. Shulkin).
An upper-extremity injury where VA switched your naturally dominant injured hand to 'Minor' after you learned to compensate with your other hand (contrary to 38 C.F.R. § 4.69).

A lower-limb amputation (at/above one knee or both ankles) missing Special Monthly Compensation, multiple annual clothing allowances (§ 3.810), or automatic secondary service connection for later heart disease under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(c).
important_cautions: Anti-stacking limits to keep in mind: while knee instability and knee motion can stack, a single shoulder cannot receive two separate Diagnostic Code 5201 ratings for flexion and abduction (Cullen v. Shinseki); non-painful X-ray-only arthritis across multiple joints under Diagnostic Code 5003 combines into a single 10% or 20% rating; and distal limb ratings cannot exceed the elective amputation ceiling in 38 C.F.R. § 4.68.

Bilateral foot ratings: when a single bilateral foot rating (such as 50% bilateral flatfoot under Diagnostic Code 5276 or 30% bilateral plantar fasciitis under Diagnostic Code 5269) is the ONLY compensable lower-extremity disability, it does not receive an extra standalone 10% bilateral factor unless another compensable lower-extremity condition exists.

Date gates and exam errors: the July 16, 2015 total-prosthesis rule (80 FR 42040; Hudgens v. McDonald) and February 7, 2021 musculoskeletal overhaul (85 FR 76453 / 86 FR 8142) depend on exact claim/decision dates, while existing ratings are protected under 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a). Incomplete joint exam testing (Correia / Sharp) is a duty-to-assist issue for open claims/appeals—not Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) under Cook v. Principi—and George v. McDonough / 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c) limit CUE motions.
VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law.
questions_for_representative: Did my VA joint examination test passive, active, weight-bearing, and opposite-joint motion (Correia v. McDonald) and estimate additional degree loss during flare-ups (DeLuca / Sharp)?

On my knee Rating Code Sheet, can instability (Diagnostic Code 5257), limited flexion (Diagnostic Code 5260), limited extension (Diagnostic Code 5261), or meniscal locking (Diagnostic Codes 5258/5259) be rated separately?
Did VA properly rate my naturally dominant arm under the 'Major' column in 38 C.F.R. § 4.69?

If I wear orthopedic braces, crutches, a walker, or prosthetics, have we checked eligibility for multiple annual clothing allowances (§ 3.810), Specially Adapted Housing (§ 3.809), or Special Monthly Compensation?
